description: Crypto deposit and withdrawal availability across exchanges, for every asset each exchange returns (omit 'assets' for all; there is no ticker list or top-N cutoff). One row per exchange, region, asset and network where the exchange states flags per network (KuCoin, Bitget, Gate, HTX, Binance, MEXC, Bybit, OKX, Upbit); otherwise one asset-level row with network null (Coinone, WhiteBIT). 'deposit' and 'withdrawal' are independent: enabled, disabled or unknown. unknown means the exchange did not state it in a documented way; a missing field, an absent asset, a failed or rate-limited request or an unrecognised value is never reported as disabled. An asset-level flag is never copied onto its networks. Rows keep the exchange's own asset and network ids and contract address where it gives one; 'network' is a canonical name matched by explicit aliases (ERC20, TRC20, BEP20...), never by ticker. 'networks' filters by alias, the exchange's own label or a contract address; asset-level rows never match it. Page with 'limit' (default 200, max 1000) and 'cursor' (next_cursor; same filters). Each row carries retrieved_at and stale: a stale row is last-known data served because the exchange failed now, with its original retrieved_at. Coverage and health are not part of the response; instead 'warnings' names every exchange that did not answer (its rows are absent, which never means disabled), that answered from stale data, that was not queried for lack of credentials, and where Gate's per-chain status was not confirmed. Keyed exchanges (Binance, MEXC, Bybit, OKX, Upbit) are not queried until the operator configures read-only keys. Status can lag the exchange by minutes; check before moving funds, never a guarantee.

assets.description: Asset symbols, e.g. ['WAVES'] or ['USDT','USDC']. Omit for every asset each exchange returns.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

exchanges.description: Exchange names or ids, e.g. ['Gate','upbit-kr']. Omit for all.

networks.description: Networks, by alias ('ERC20', 'Tron'), the exchange's own label, or a contract address. Omit for all.

name: exchange_wallet_status

network.description: Canonical network, when the aliases match; null for an asset-level row or an unrecognised label

network_id.description: The exchange's own network id; null when the exchange states no per-network flags

total.description: Rows matching the filters across all pages
